newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: 74 NZ work stoppages end in yr to July 1996 - SNZ.
newsitem.headline: 74 NZ work stoppages end in yr to July 1996 - SNZ.

text.p: Thirteen work stoppages ended in the month of July, 1996, Statisitics New Zealand said on Wednesday.

Of these, 10 were complete strikes, two were partial strikes and one was a complete lockout. Together these involved 19,431 employees and resulted in the loss of 13,734 person-days of work and about NZ$2.375 million in wages and salaries, SNZ said.
"There were 74 stoppages ending in the 12 months to July 31, 1996, the highest number of stoppages ending in a 12 month period since the 12 months to October 1991," SNZ said.
Stoppages that ended in the year to 31 July 1996 involved 33,926 employees, more than the 32,811 involved in the year to July 1995 and the 15,503 in the year to July 1994.
An estimated $6.1 million was lost by employees in the July 1996 year, compared with $6.9 million in the July 1995 year and $4.6 million in the July 1994 year.
SNZ said 26 of the 74 stoppages recorded in the year to July 1996 occurred in the manufacturing industry. A further 16 occurred in the education industry.
In the year to July 1996, 39 stoppages occurred in the private sector while 35 occurred in the public sector.

"Total public sector losses of both person-days of work and wages and salaries were higher than private sector losses. However, losses of both person-days of work and wages and salaries per employee were greater in the private sector," SNZ said.
As well as the 13 stoppages ending in July 1996, 10 others were still in progress.
